content:
incident-bot: ALERT: GPU queue length > 95th pct threshold in us-west-2 (driver/runtime errors increasing). Auto-pager fired for SLO impact. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/gpu/queue?range=15m :rotating_light:
maeve: I’m on it. seeing queue growth from ~800 -> 6.2k in 10m. latency SLOs tripping for /v1/generate. paging now.
anika: thanks. any immediate customer-facing impact? cust-ops?
cust-ops: a couple PLG customers reported timeouts for heavy-batch endpoints. no major enterprise pages yet but CS has a ticket from alpha-ops about retries.
ricardo: adding runtime logs. kernel Xid spikes, repeated GPU driver disconnects, and some OOM-kill traces on the node set handling the pt-quantized models. snippet: ```[timestamp] NVRM: Xid (79): GPU page fault at 0x7ff...
[...]
[ 12345.678901] Out of memory: Killed process 23456 (model-worker) total-vm:2048m```.
maeve: are we hitting cloud quota for new nodes when autoscaler tries to add? check autoscaler events pls.
ricardo: checking HPA/cluster-autoscaler events... `kubectl -n runtime describe hpa gpupool` -> shows scale-up requests, but `cluster-autoscaler` logs: `Scale-up rejected: quota exceeded for nvidia-a100` and `FailedToAcquire: insufficient accelerators available in region us-west-2`.
anika: so two parallel failure modes: driver instability causing effective capacity drop -> backlog; autoscaler can't replace because of quota/stock; result = sustained queue.
maeve: immediate mitigations: 1) route heavy requests to fallback smaller models in eu-west for non-latency-sensitive customers, 2) enable degraded-mode: reduce batch sizes + force-prefill off for heavy routes, 3) cordon and reboot suspect nodes one-by-one to clear driver state.
ricardo: working on a rolling-driver-restart plan. command to identify hot nodes: `kubectl get pods -n runtime -o wide | grep model-worker | awk '{print $7}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr` then `kubectl drain <node> --force --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` -> reboot -> uncordon. will do in small windows to avoid mass capacity loss.
deploy-bot: FYI scheduled canary rollout of kernel-driver-460.79 was completed 2h ago on subset; rollout target: all compute nodes by midnight. No correlation flagged earlier.
maeve: do NOT continue the kernel rollout until we validate. pause immediately. @deploy-bot pause rollout.
deploy-bot: Rollout paused per request (job id: r12345).
tariq: product question — what's the customer impact window? we need an ETA to share with CS.
cust-ops: currently ~35% of requests to heavy endpoints are timing out or failing with 502. impact window started ~ +00:08 and still ongoing. customers in us-west primarily.
ricardo: timeline: start investigating driver reconnects at +00:02, observed mass Xid events +00:05, autoscaler scale-up attempts at +00:06 but rejected for quota. mitigation ETA: node reboots will start now, first batch in ~5m, expect partial relief in 15-25m if driver restarts succeed. full restore depends on capacity—if quota not freed we'll stay degraded.
anika: handoff protocol: maeve remains incident lead for next 20m; ricardo will own runtime mitigation actions; after 20m, on-call shift goes to night oncall (maeve -> anika) unless resolved. update in 15m or at major milestone.
maeve: action list: 
- ricardo: start cordon+reboot of 2 hottest nodes (staggered). log reboot outputs to #eng-runtime.
- anika: authorize fallback routing to eu-west for non-US customers and update rate-limiting rules to protect control-plane.
- cust-ops: notify impacted customers with initial note: we are investigating GPU capacity issues causing timeouts; mitigation in progress.
- deploy-bot: ensure kernel rollout stays paused.
ricardo: starting cordon on node gpu-node-37 (reason: repeated Xid, mem pressure). command: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-37 && kubectl drain gpu-node-37 --grace-period=60 --timeout=10m --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` then reboot via BMC. posting output here.
maeve: note: ensure model-routing config has fallback-safety: `routes/heavy -> replica-set: low-priority, cpus-only` if autoscale can't replenish.
ricardo: drain started. encountered a stuck daemonset on pod model-cache; using `--force` allowed eviction. reboot initiated.
maeve: we should also flip cache TTL down to reduce memory pressure across nodes. anika, can you do?
anika: lowering model-cache TTL from 6h -> 30m on runtime-config. applying now: `kubectl apply -f runtime/configs/cache-ttl.yaml` done.
cust-ops: first customer notification sent. asked to escalate if any SLA critical customers see degradation.
ricardo: reboot completed for gpu-node-37, driver reinitialized. initial logs: `NVRM: Xid (31): GPU reset completed` no further OOM in dmesg for that node. queue for affected pool dropped from 6200 -> 4200 (partial). moving to gpu-node-42 next.
maeve: great. add note: if reboots don't stabilize, we may need to temporarily route a subset of traffic to Dedicated pools in other regions (requires billing approval).
tariq: ok start drafting customer update with estimated timeline 1-2 hours for full recovery, likely partial relief in 20-40m.
anika: bringing in infra to look at quota—@cloud-ops we need a manual quota bump for `nvidia-a100` or patch routing to multi-region pools.
ricardo: second node reboot done. queue now 2100 and latency percentiles improving. autoscaler still reporting `quota exceeded` for further scale-up but backlog is decreasing.
maeve: if metrics continue to improve over next 15m we can normalise and close pager. keep monitoring and post a postmortem template.
incident-bot: NOTE: Pager closed (acknowledged). Please file incident report with timeline, root cause hypotheses (driver instability + quota limits), and remediation actions.
maeve: assigning follow-ups: 
- ricardo: collect driver logs and correlate kernel rollout (if any) + device firmware versions.
- anika: run chaos test on smaller cluster to reproduce Xid pattern (non-prod).
- cust-ops: compile customer impact list and send formal update.
- tariq: own comms and postmortem stub.
maeve: handing off to anika for night coverage in 20m per plan. everyone stay in thread for updates. :thumbsup:
